headline: Profit rebounds sharply, guidance raised again
summary_short: Lockheed Martin grew Q2 FY2026 sales 10.5% y/y to $20,063M and net earnings surged to $1,836M ($7.94 diluted EPS) from $342M ($1.46) a year ago, since the prior-year quarter absorbed $1.6B of program reach-forward losses; the company raised its full-year 2026 sales, segment profit, EPS, and free-cash-flow guidance.
summary_long: Sales rose 10.5% y/y on growth across all four segments (Missiles and Fire Control +19%, Aeronautics +9%, Rotary and Mission Systems +9%, Space +6%) driven by munitions ramps and F-35 volume. Consolidated operating profit jumped 231% y/y to $2,479M, mostly because the year-ago quarter absorbed $1.6B of reach-forward losses on a classified Aeronautics program and the CMHP/TUHP helicopter programs; margin reached 12.4% from 4.1%. Net earnings were $1,836M ($7.94 diluted EPS) versus $342M a year ago. Cash from operations more than doubled to $3.2B and free cash flow was $2.9B on faster customer receipts. Backlog hit a record $230.4B after a $35B THAAD contract. Lockheed raised FY2026 guidance for sales, segment operating profit, EPS, and free cash flow.

drivers.explanation: Sales grew across all four segments: Missiles and Fire Control +19% on PAC-3/THAAD and PrSM production ramps, Aeronautics +9% mainly on higher F-35 production volume, Rotary and Mission Systems +9%, and Space +6% on Fleet Ballistic Missile and Next Generation Interceptor volume.
Net earnings increased $1.5B and diluted EPS rose $6.48, primarily due to higher consolidated operating profit of $1.7B, partially offset by a $267M increase in income tax expense.
Tracks the diluted-EPS move described above; basic EPS is marginally higher on a slightly smaller basic share count (230.2M vs 231.1M diluted).
Reflects the $1.7B higher operating profit, partly offset by a $267M higher income tax expense; the effective tax rate fell to 15.7% from 18.0% on lower interest expense on uncertain tax positions.

Increased $1.7B largely because the year-ago quarter included $1.6B of reach-forward losses (a classified Aeronautics program plus CMHP and TUHP helicopter programs), a $66M prior-year asset write-off, and a $43M higher FAS/CAS adjustment.
Cost of revenue grew only 1.1% versus 10.5% sales growth because the year-ago quarter's cost of revenue absorbed the $1.6B of reach-forward loss charges that did not recur this quarter.
Tracks the consolidated operating-profit increase described above; other income, net was roughly flat ($33M vs $14M) and does not materially change the picture.
Tracks the operating-profit increase; depreciation and amortization was a relatively stable add-back year over year ($798M vs $796M on a six-month basis).

Rose only 1.1% despite 10.5% sales growth because the year-ago quarter's cost of revenue included the $1.6B of reach-forward loss charges on the classified Aeronautics and CMHP/TUHP programs that did not recur.
Tracks the operating-profit increase; interest expense was roughly flat ($266M vs $274M) and other non-operating income rose slightly ($45M vs $42M).

Cash from operations and free cash flow each rose about $3.0B primarily due to the timing of customer receipts and lower tax payments; the quarter included $318M of capex and $558M of independent R&D spending.

Current maturities of long-term debt fell to $0 from $3,118M a year ago; $1,168M of long-term debt was repaid year-to-date per the cash-flow statement, but the release does not separately explain the reclassification.

Rose to $8,768M from $5,334M, consistent with retained-earnings growth from $3,324M of six-month net income, partly offset by $1,612M of dividends paid year-to-date; not separately explained in the release.
No share repurchases occurred in the first half of 2026 per the cash-flow statement, so the y/y decline in diluted share count reflects 2025 buyback activity rather than any current-period action.

CEO Jim Taiclet cited $65 billion of new orders lifting backlog to a record $230 billion and said results give "confidence to raise our full year financial guidance," now anticipating ~8% accelerated sales growth, 28% higher segment operating profit, and free cash flow over $7 billion.

FY2026 guidance was raised for sales ($79,750-$81,750M from $77,500-$80,000M), business segment operating profit ($8,500-$8,700M from $8,425-$8,675M), diluted EPS ($29.95-$30.65 from $29.35-$30.25), and free cash flow ($7,000-$7,200M from $6,500-$6,800M, matching the CEO's explicit 'over $7 billion' quote); capex guidance was lowered ($2,000-$2,400M from $2,500-$2,800M). These five were written to the event's guidance[] array with move accordingly. Two guidance lines were captured with move=null rather than inferred: the FAS/CAS pension adjustment shows an identical ~$1,365M in both the 'Current Update' and 'April 2026' columns, but the release never uses reaffirmation language ('unchanged', 'reaffirmed', 'on track') for this line, so per the hard rule that silence is not reaffirmation, no move was assigned; cash from operations guidance narrowed ($9,200-$9,400M from $9,150-$9,450M) with an unchanged $9,300M midpoint -- the low end rose but the high end fell, which is neither a clean raise nor a clean lower, so it was left unmoved rather than mischaracterized.
